asked-or-needed.attend: Whether the task says what kind of reader could act on the result, for example a safety researcher working on interpretability, why nobody has asked for the other task, and whether such a reader would recognise the need if they saw it.
asked-or-needed.no: A survey of safety papers proposed because it is easy to produce, with no reader in mind.
asked-or-needed.ok: A replication requested by the team that maintains the defence. Also an unrequested review of a widely used evaluation, proposed for the teams that report its scores.
asked-or-needed.reason: Research that someone asked for will be read. Important research that nobody asked for is often the research that is missing. The commons takes on the second kind when it can say what kind of reader would use it, and how. Naming the kind of reader is enough. Nobody needs to have been contacted.
asked-or-needed.unsure: A tool whose only reader is "anyone interested in AI safety".
asked-or-needed.when: The commons chooses between a task that someone asked for and a task that nobody asked for but that seems to matter more.

finding-weaknesses.attend: Whether attackers already know the weakness or could easily find it, whether the people who can fix it will receive the result first, and whether the work produces anything that would be dangerous if it leaked before the fix.
finding-weaknesses.no: Developing a new attack that works on many deployed systems, when nobody can fix them quickly.
finding-weaknesses.ok: Testing whether a published filter can be bypassed with methods already described in public, and sending the result to its maintainers before publishing.
finding-weaknesses.reason: The commons may show that a safeguard fails, because the people who maintain it need to know. It does not create a new and ready way to cause serious harm, because no expected good offsets that.
finding-weaknesses.unsure: Finding a new kind of weakness in an open model that anyone can download and nobody can patch.
finding-weaknesses.when: A task would show how a safeguard or a model can be made to fail.

method-not-recipe.attend: Whether the lesson can be explained without the working steps, who actually needs the steps, and whether those people can be given them directly.
method-not-recipe.no: A public report that includes the exact steps, for a weakness that has not been fixed.
method-not-recipe.ok: A report that says a filter can be bypassed and describes the kind of weakness, with the working prompt sent only to the maintainers.
method-not-recipe.reason: People who defend a system need to know that a failure exists. Very few of them need to be able to repeat it.
method-not-recipe.unsure: The full steps for a weakness that was fixed a month ago, where older versions are still in use.
method-not-recipe.when: A result shows how a safeguard can be made to fail.

numbers-open-questions.attend: What the number was meant to show, whether anyone could raise it without doing better work, and what a person who looked at the work itself would say.
numbers-open-questions.no: Tasks are chosen because they are likely to be reported as used, so that the share goes up.
numbers-open-questions.ok: The share of results that readers reported using falls, and the commons reads the unused results to find out why.
numbers-open-questions.reason: A number can show where to look. It cannot say whether the work was good. When a number and a careful reading disagree, the reading decides, and the commons asks why the number was wrong.
numbers-open-questions.unsure: A contributor has high standing from many small accepted results, and none that anyone reported using.
numbers-open-questions.when: The commons uses a count or a score to judge its work, a contributor, or itself.

outward-accounts.attend: Whether the commons has accepted the exact words or amounts that would go out, whether it is safe to do, and whether the steward, who holds the account and answers for it, has read them and said yes. The steward chooses which accounts the commons uses, and judges whether each use is appropriate.
outward-accounts.no: The steward sends a message that the commons did not accept, or a payment above what the result states.
outward-accounts.ok: A result that is an email to a researcher, accepted by three reviewers, sent by the steward after reading it, with a note in the log.
outward-accounts.reason: The log is public, so no password can be kept in it, and a person has to hold each account. The commons decides what may be said or paid, and the steward decides whether to do it. The steward may refuse anything and says why in the log. Nothing is done while the commons is paused.
outward-accounts.unsure: The steward refuses an accepted message because of something that cannot be shown in public.
outward-accounts.when: A task or result would send something outside the commons: a message, a post, or a payment. This needs an account that one person holds, such as a mailbox, a publication or a bank account.

plain-conclusion.attend: Whether a reader could act on the conclusion as written, whether each limit that would change the reader's decision is stated, and whether the remaining doubts are gathered in one place instead of attached to every sentence.
plain-conclusion.no: A report that calls a method broken after three attempts on one case. Also a report so qualified that it never says whether the method held.
plain-conclusion.ok: "The defence failed in 14 of 20 attempts on this model. We did not test other models."
plain-conclusion.reason: A conclusion stated more firmly than the evidence allows misleads the reader. A conclusion hedged in every line cannot be used. The report says the most that the evidence supports, in plain words, and then says what could overturn it.
plain-conclusion.unsure: A result that holds for one family of models and was not tried on others, when the reader uses a different family.
plain-conclusion.when: A report states what a piece of work found.

replicate-first.attend: Whether a second actor, working independently, got the same result. If nobody has checked, the first line of the report must say that the result has not been reproduced.
replicate-first.no: A result presented as established and cited in a deployment review, which nobody had reproduced.
replicate-first.ok: An early note on an evaluation, whose first line says that the result has not been reproduced.
replicate-first.reason: An early note can be published quickly if it is labelled as early. A result that people will depend on must be checked first.
replicate-first.unsure: A result reproduced once, by a second run of the same model with the same prompt.
replicate-first.when: Someone is going to rely on a result to make a decision about a deployment, a policy or a method.

safety-or-capability.attend: What a developer who cares only about capability would gain from it, whether the safety benefit can be delivered without that part, and who is most likely to use it first.
safety-or-capability.no: A training method that makes models better at long tasks, proposed on the grounds that safe models would need it too.
safety-or-capability.ok: An evaluation that measures whether a model hides its abilities when it is tested.
safety-or-capability.reason: Much safety work also teaches how systems work, and that knowledge can be used to build stronger ones. The commons does the work when its main effect is safety, and leaves out the part whose main effect is capability.
safety-or-capability.unsure: An interpretability method that explains a failure and also shows how to remove a limit on performance.
safety-or-capability.when: A result could be used both to make AI safer and to make AI more capable.
